commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Zucc
commitResults.messageBody: Keep the Java entry point, startup banner, setup instructions, and user guide consistent with the new chatbot name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add initial chatbot greeting and farewell
commitResults.messageBody: Display the Zucc banner and framed welcome and exit messages so the starter application meets the required interaction flow.
Read and echo commands until EOF, exit on bye, and use try-with-resources so the input scanner is always closed.
Route the banner, greeting, echoed commands, and farewell through one formatter so all output follows the required indentation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add in-memory task storage and listing
commitResults.messageBody: Store up to 100 user-entered tasks and display them in insertion order when the list command is used.
Track completion state alongside tasks, support mark commands, and display checkbox status in task listings.
Support unmark commands by clearing a task's completion state and displaying its updated status.
Encapsulate each task's description and completion state in a dedicated class, and refactor Zucc to use Task objects for listing, marking, and unmarking.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add end-to-end support for todo tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Parse todo commands into Todo objects so undated tasks have a distinct type marker while retaining Task completion behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add end-to-end support for deadline tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Parse deadline commands at the /by separator and preserve supplied deadline text literally. Add a temporary rejection stub for commands that omit /by so they do not crash the application.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add end-to-end support for event tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Parse event commands at the /from and /to separators and preserve both date or time values literally. Add temporary rejection stubs for missing separators so malformed events do not crash the application.
Share task storage and confirmation to remove duplicated logic. Note that option parsing remains command-specific for now, allowing each task type's date and time syntax to evolve independently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid task numbers in mark and unmark commands

commitResults.messageBody: Following the mark and unmark validation change, recognize bare todo, deadline, and event command words too. This gives all argument-taking commands consistent handling, provides command-specific guidance for missing arguments, and rejects truly unknown input instead of storing it as a task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Validate required deadline and event fields
commitResults.messageBody: After recognizing bare task command words consistently, ensure dated tasks are complete before storing them. Deadlines now require a description and /by value, while events require a description plus /from and /to values.

Now that only valid task commands reach the shared insertion path, enforce the fixed 100-task limit there. The chatbot reports the limit and continues running instead of writing beyond the task array.
Enforce completion-state rules in the task model itself. Repeated mark or unmark commands now report the existing state instead of silently pretending a change occurred.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add some personality to validation errors

commitResults.messageBody:
Users need to remove tasks that are no longer relevant while keeping the displayed task numbers accurate.

Replace the fixed-size task array with an ArrayList to support dynamic storage and straightforward removal. Add the delete command with task-number validation, removal confirmation, and an updated task count.

This also removes the previous 100-task limit and fulfills the requirement to use Java Collections for task storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor command parsing into typed input
commitResults.messageBody:
The main loop previously mixed raw-string recognition, command-specific splitting, validation, and task execution. This duplicated parsing rules across branches and made new commands or options harder to add consistently.

Introduce CommandType and ParsedCommand so input is parsed once into a known command, a main argument, and generic /option value pairs. Preserve embedded spacing and report missing, duplicate, or unsupported input consistently through ZuccException, while keeping command dispatch explicit in Zucc.

Move required-field validation into task constructors so task validity does not depend on the CLI code path. This prevents incomplete Todo, Deadline, and Event objects from being created by future callers.

Load saved tasks when Zucc starts and save the list after each
successful mutation.

Centralize file-format encoding and decoding in Task, while concrete
task constructors validate decoded field arrays using Java 25
constructor prologues.

Move the task list and storage into a Zucc instance so every
state mutation remains paired with a save.

Expose task operations as the object's public API while keeping CLI
parsing private and use toString to format the numbered task list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse task dates and times into typed values
commitResults.messageBody:
Store deadline and event dates as LocalDateTime instead of raw strings.
Centralize parsing and formatting, reject invalid event ranges, and
document the accepted date-time format.

Add an on command that shows deadlines and events occurring on a given
date. Define date matching across task subclasses, reuse task-list
formatting without mutable filter state, and document the date-only
command format.

Move task ownership, validation, mutation, counting, and formatting out
of Zucc into a dedicated TaskList class.

Allow Storage to persist tasks through a structurally read-only Iterable
interface, avoiding exposure of TaskList's backing collection while
keeping persistence separate from task management.

Move command-line input, framed output formatting, the greeting, and
scanner cleanup from Zucc into a dedicated Ui class.

Keep command handling and command-specific response construction in Zucc
so this increment changes only the terminal interaction boundary.

Move command recognition, input tokenization, named-option collection,
duplicate-option detection, and task-number conversion into a dedicated
Parser class.

Keep ParsedCommand focused on storing parsed values and enforcing
command-specific usage rules, while Zucc delegates interpretation of raw
user input.

Move command processing from the static entry point into an instance run
method and provide the Ui as an interactive-session dependency.

Keep Zucc construction focused on loading persistent task state while
reducing main to resource management, startup-error handling, and
application launch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command handling into command classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Parse user input directly into concrete Command subclasses and move
command-specific validation and behavior out of Zucc.

Centralize argument and option handling in Command, including required
values, duplicate options, unsupported options, and commands without
positional arguments.

Expose Command.parse as the creation boundary, restrict direct
construction, and remove the intermediate ParsedCommand and CommandType
representations.

Move command, task, storage, and UI classes into cohesive subpackages
while keeping the application coordinator and shared exception in zucc.
Preserve package-private collaboration where possible and update the
README entry-point path.

Configure Gradle to launch zucc.Zucc so the run task and executable JAR
work with the current package structure.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add focused JUnit coverage for core task behavior
commitResults.messageBody:
Test command parsing, task validation and state changes, date handling,
list operations, serialization, storage failures, and robustness edge
cases to protect the application's main business logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename fat JAR output to match project
commitResults.messageBody:
Configure the Shadow JAR task to use the project name, making the
packaged application easier to identify and run.
